name: Bicep: weakened access control (ACR admin / Key Vault RBAC off)
attack_scenario: the shared ACR admin password leaks from a pipeline or the broad Key Vault access policy is abused, and the attacker pushes a poisoned image or reads every secret in the vault with no way to trace which identity did it
negative_test_hint: deploy a template containing "adminUserEnabled: true" and assert the policy check fails and the shared registry admin credential is never created

exemplar.explanation: adminUserEnabled:true turns on a single shared registry admin credential (no per-identity attribution, cannot be scoped) instead of AAD/token auth; enableRbacAuthorization:false makes Key Vault fall back to legacy vault access policies that grant coarse, hard-to-audit permissions. CIS Azure recommends the admin account off and RBAC on.
